note: NOT here: replacing the TIME answer's `(int)(double)` chain with a plain `(int)`.  It was written, run and WITHDRAWN as uncatchable: the two spellings agree exactly for every answer below 2^31, and above it the conversion is undefined in C -- the x87 answers 0x80000000 and GCC 14 folds the chain away entirely (finding F8755).  A mutant that can only be caught by probing undefined behaviour is not a claim this suite can hold.  The chain is carried by the disassembly at 0xb05a3 (`fildll` on a zero-extended doubleword) and 0xb05c2 (a truncating `fistpl`).

note: NOT here: removing silence_create's `if (s == 0) return 0` after the allocation.  The harness allocator never fails on request, so the arm is unreachable from any fixture and the mutant would read NOT CAUGHT while modelling nothing -- see t_fdspksil.c's header.  It is carried by the disassembly at 0xb03f8 (`xor %eax,%eax; test %edx,%edx; jne`), which is also what distinguishes silence_create from FIFO8_create, whose allocation is NOT checked.

NOT here: advancing `out` between silence_progress's two escapes.  That is deviation D983 -- the object does NOT advance it, and a mutant that fixed the overwrite would be testing our opinion of the bug rather than the object's behaviour.  The 1700-sample calls in t_fdspksil compare the whole destination buffer against the blob's, so the overwrite is reproduced and would be caught if it stopped being.

silence_level_table's three live rows, one ULP each, and EXACTLY ONE DIRECTION PER ROW IS CATCHABLE.  They are here because the suite otherwise reached the table only through `the threshold test runs the wrong way round`, which moves the COMPARISON and not the CONSTANTS -- a wrong word in the table was covered by nothing.  Finding F8747 has the measurement.

label: silence level 1 is one ULP high

silence level 3 is one ULP high

note: THE OTHER THREE DIRECTIONS ARE UNCATCHABLE AND WERE MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED -- registering them would put three permanent NOT CAUGHT rows in the gate. The threshold branch `acc > silence_level_table[lvl]` catches NONE of the six: the value reaching it is a block sum times 0.00125, a map that steps by about 1.28 ULP and therefore SKIPS floats, so a one-ULP move of the threshold has no preimage on either side.  Every one of the three above is caught by the DEBUG LINE instead, and only because it crosses an integer there: the object multiplies the row by SILENCE_FULLSCALE2 at 80-bit precision (exact) and truncates toward zero, so the printed values are 2699, 7500 and 24299 from exact products 2699.999989942, 7500.000216186 and 24299.999177098.  Rows 1 and 3 sit just BELOW an integer, so only a step UP crosses it; row 2 sits just ABOVE one, so only a step DOWN does.  An earlier reading of this had rows 1 and 3 catchable both ways and row 2 high as the single gap; running it says otherwise, and the run is what is recorded.
